title: Composing functors on sequences with varying coefficient categories
statement:
For $n\ge1$, let $\mathcal A_n,\mathcal B_n,\mathcal C_n$ be categories, with functors $S_n^{\mathcal A}:\mathcal A_n\to\mathcal A_{n+1}$ and similarly $S_n^{\mathcal B},S_n^{\mathcal C}$. Write $\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal A,S^{\mathcal A})$ for the category whose objects are families $H_n\in\mathcal A_n$ with arrows $h_n:H_{n+1}\to S_n^{\mathcal A}H_n$, and whose morphisms $a:(H,h)\to(H',h')$ are families $a_n:H_n\to H'_n$ satisfying $S_n^{\mathcal A}(a_n)h_n=h'_na_{n+1}$; identities and composition are componentwise. Use the analogous categories for $\mathcal B,\mathcal C$; this extends the inverse-system convention of [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $J_n:\mathcal A_n\to\mathcal B_n$ and $D_n:\mathcal B_n\to\mathcal C_n$ be functors equipped with specified natural isomorphisms
$$e_n:J_{n+1}S_n^{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n^{\mathcal B}J_n,\qquad c_n:D_{n+1}S_n^{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n^{\mathcal C}D_n.$$
Then there are functors $\widehat J:\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal A,S^{\mathcal A})\to\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal B,S^{\mathcal B})$ and $\widehat D:\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal B,S^{\mathcal B})\to\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal C,S^{\mathcal C})$, with levels $J_nH_n,D_nL_n$, transitions $e_n(H_n)J_{n+1}(h_n),c_n(L_n)D_{n+1}(d_n)$, and component maps $J_n(a_n),D_n(a_n)$, respectively. Their composite has level $D_nJ_nH_n$ and transition
$$v_n=c_n(J_nH_n)\circ D_{n+1}(e_n(H_n))\circ D_{n+1}(J_{n+1}(h_n)).$$
For every $\alpha:(L,d)\to\widehat J(H,h)$ in $\operatorname{Seq}(\mathcal B,S^{\mathcal B})$, set $b_n=D_n(\alpha_n)$ and $u_n=c_n(L_n)D_{n+1}(d_n)$. Then
$$S_n^{\mathcal C}(b_n)\circ u_n=v_n\circ b_{n+1}.$$
The composite functor agrees with the sequence functor for $D_nJ_n$ equipped with the pasted coefficient comparison $c_n(J_n(-))\circ D_{n+1}(e_n(-))$, on objects, transitions and morphisms. All functors preserve componentwise isomorphisms. No common category for the different levels and no strict lift of these objects from a derived category is assumed.

proof.text:
The convention of [def-weil-inverse-system] is recovered when all level categories coincide and all $S_n$ are identities. For varying levels, identity families satisfy the required squares because $S_n(1)=1$. If $a:H\to H'$ and $a':H'\to H''$ satisfy the squares, then
$$S_n(a'_na_n)h_n=S_n(a'_n)S_n(a_n)h_n=S_n(a'_n)h'_na_{n+1}=h''_na'_{n+1}a_{n+1}.$$
Thus componentwise composition is defined; its associativity and units hold at each level. This verifies that each stated sequence category is a category.

source.place: Tag 0030 (definition-system-over-poset), with the varying-level category checked directly

proof.text:
Put $t_n=e_n(H_n)J_{n+1}(h_n)$ and $t'_n=e_n(H'_n)J_{n+1}(h'_n)$. For a sequence morphism $a$, naturality of $e_n$, followed by its given square, gives
$$S_n^{\mathcal B}(J_n(a_n))t_n=e_n(H'_n)J_{n+1}(S_n^{\mathcal A}(a_n))J_{n+1}(h_n)=e_n(H'_n)J_{n+1}(h'_n)J_{n+1}(a_{n+1})=t'_nJ_{n+1}(a_{n+1}).$$
Every factor lies in $\mathcal B_{n+1}$. Hence the displayed component maps define morphisms. The equations $J_n(1)=1$ and $J_n(a'_na_n)=J_n(a'_n)J_n(a_n)$ verify the functor laws for $\widehat J$. The same calculation with $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,J,e)$ replaced by $(\mathcal B,\mathcal C,D,c)$ defines $\widehat D$. Its object transition is $c_n(L_n)D_{n+1}(d_n)$ as asserted.

proof.text:
Evaluate $\widehat D\widehat J$ on $(H,h)$. Its level is $D_nJ_nH_n$; its transition is
$$c_n(J_nH_n)D_{n+1}(e_n(H_n)J_{n+1}(h_n))=c_n(J_nH_n)D_{n+1}(e_n(H_n))D_{n+1}(J_{n+1}(h_n))=v_n,$$
by the composition law for $D_{n+1}$. For the specified $\alpha$ its input square is $S_n^{\mathcal B}(\alpha_n)d_n=e_n(H_n)J_{n+1}(h_n)\alpha_{n+1}$. Naturality of $c_n$ and this square give
$$S_n^{\mathcal C}(D_n\alpha_n)c_n(L_n)D_{n+1}(d_n)=c_n(J_nH_n)D_{n+1}(S_n^{\mathcal B}(\alpha_n)d_n)=v_nD_{n+1}(\alpha_{n+1}).$$
The ends are maps $D_{n+1}L_{n+1}\to S_n^{\mathcal C}D_nJ_nH_n$ in $\mathcal C_{n+1}$, proving the requested equation for $b_n,u_n$.

proof.text:
Define $p_n(H)=c_n(J_nH)D_{n+1}(e_n(H))$. For any $a:H\to H'$ in $\mathcal A_n$, naturality of $c_n$ then of $e_n$ gives
$$S_n^{\mathcal C}(D_nJ_n(a))p_n(H)=c_n(J_nH')D_{n+1}(S_n^{\mathcal B}(J_n(a))e_n(H))=p_n(H')D_{n+1}(J_{n+1}(S_n^{\mathcal A}(a))).$$
Thus $p_n$ is natural. Its component inverse is $D_{n+1}(e_n(H)^{-1})c_n(J_nH)^{-1}$: both composites cancel to identities by the functor laws. The preceding naturality equation, multiplied by the component inverses, gives naturality of the inverse. Therefore $p_n$ is the required coefficient comparison isomorphism. The construction checked in Step 2, applied to $D_nJ_n,p_n$, has transitions $p_n(H_n)D_{n+1}J_{n+1}(h_n)=v_n$ and arrows $D_nJ_n(a_n)$. These are precisely the composite functor's data, so the functors agree.

proof.text:
If a sequence morphism $a:(H,h)\to(H',h')$ has invertible components, multiplying its square by inverses gives
$$S_n(a_n^{-1})h'_n=h_na_{n+1}^{-1}.$$
Here $S_n(a_n^{-1})$ is inverse to $S_n(a_n)$ because $S_n$ preserves their two identity composites. Thus $(a_n^{-1})$ is a sequence morphism and its two composites with $a$ are the identity families. Each $J_n(a_n)$ has inverse $J_n(a_n^{-1})$ by the same functor laws, and likewise for $D_n$ and $D_nJ_n$. This proves preservation of componentwise isomorphisms for all the asserted functors. Every calculation took place at a single level; no common ambient category or strict derived lift was used.
